title: Point-to-Point vs Publish-Subscribe Messaging
description: Compare point-to-point and publish-subscribe messaging patterns, understand their trade-offs, and learn when to use each.

data.text: Message-driven systems use two fundamental patterns: point-to-point and publish-subscribe (pub/sub). Choosing the right pattern affects coupling, scalability, and observability. Point-to-point routes a message to exactly one consumer, while pub/sub broadcasts to all interested consumers.

In point-to-point messaging, a producer sends a message to a specific queue, and exactly one consumer receives and processes it. If multiple consumers listen on the same queue, they compete for messages in a load-balanced fashion. This pattern is ideal for task distribution, background job processing, and command-style operations where one handler should process each message.

In pub/sub, a producer publishes an event to a topic, and every subscription receives a copy of the message. This allows many independent consumers to react to the same event without the producer knowing about them. Pub/sub is ideal for event broadcasting, audit logging, and data synchronization across multiple bounded contexts.

cards.title: Point-to-Point
cards.description: One producer, one queue, one consumer per message

cards.title: Publish-Subscribe
cards.description: One producer, one topic, many consumers
pros: Loose coupling between producer and consumers
Consumers can be added or removed independently
cons: Message delivered to all subscribers (higher cost)

data.text: In RabbitMQ, point-to-point is achieved by binding a direct exchange to a single queue. When multiple consumers share the same queue, RabbitMQ distributes messages in a round-robin fashion, ensuring each message is processed exactly once.

data.text: Implementing Pub-Sub with Azure Service Bus Topics

Azure Service Bus topics implement pub/sub natively. A publisher sends once, and each subscription receives a full copy. Subscriptions can filter messages using SQL expressions, so each consumer only gets the events it cares about while sharing the same topic.

data.title: Use the Right Pattern for the Right Job
data.text: Use point-to-point for commands and tasks (e.g., ProcessOrderCommand). Use pub/sub for events and notifications (e.g., OrderCreatedEvent). Commands have one handler; events have multiple interested parties.

items.question: Can I combine both patterns?
items.answer: Yes. Use point-to-point for command messages that trigger a single action, and pub/sub for domain events that multiple services need to react to. Most real systems use both.

items.question: Does pub/sub mean every subscriber gets every message?
items.answer: By default, yes. However, brokers like SNS, Service Bus topics, and RabbitMQ topic exchanges allow filtering so subscribers only receive relevant messages.

items.question: What about request-reply over messaging?
items.answer: Request-reply is a separate pattern. The sender adds a reply-to address and correlation ID to the message headers, then listens on a temporary queue for the response.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Point-to-point delivers to one consumer; good for commands and tasks
Pub/sub broadcasts to all subscribers; good for events and notifications
Service Bus topics and RabbitMQ topic/fanout exchanges implement pub/sub
data.takeaway: Choose point-to-point for single-handler tasks; choose pub/sub when multiple systems need to react to the same event.
